structured.approach: I loaded the backend-steps procedure for BE-02 and read feat.tasks to find the Backend tasks. These are TSK-05 and TSK-06, both in ap_aging, and both are pure functions with no transport layer. I searched the ap_aging repository for any secret use (environment variables, tokens, passwords, HTTP clients) and found none. I also read aging.py and ci.py to confirm that the code and CI need no credentials. I then compared what the tasks need (nothing) with the permission table's grant through the tool view (nothing), and wrote task.secrets_scope with secret names only. I made no access requests because none were needed. I did not use the osv or pypi connectors because they have nothing to do with secrets.

claims.text: The Backend tasks for FEAT-ZD-48600 are TSK-05 (STORY-05) and TSK-06 (STORY-06), both in the ap_aging repository.
TSK-05 adds a pure function overdue_with_risk(invoices, as_of, risk_by_vendor), and TSK-06 adds overdue_rows_to_json(rows) with no transport layer, because a transport would re-trigger DES-01.
The tasks add no new technology beyond the Python 3.9 standard library.
The current ap_aging source imports only datetime, decimal and typing, and the repository does not read environment variables, tokens, passwords or HTTP clients.
CI runs locally with ci.py (compile, unit tests, coverage gate, static checks) and uses no credentials.
No secrets are required or granted for ap_aging under the permission table, so required and granted access match and no access request is needed.
The only external-provider touchpoint in the feature is TSK-04 in the Data Science lane (acme-llm, pending TQ-8), which is outside Backend scope.

structured.summary: The Backend tasks TSK-05 and TSK-06 in ap_aging don't need any secrets. They are pure Python standard-library functions with no network, database or configuration access, and the ap_aging permission table grants none. Required and granted access match (none and none), so I raised no access requests and found nothing to flag for revocation. The secrets scope is written to outputs/FEAT-ZD-48600/task.secrets_scope.md (names only, no values). There are no open questions.
